<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)

No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ### ① Derived judgments

**Shape.** The one change is the primary-subtag width, `{2,8}` to `{2,3}`; every other part of the grammar (`(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*`, both anchors, no flags) is byte-unchanged. The claim that "BCP-47 reserves 4 letters and registers no 5–8 letter language" is accurate (RFC 5646 §2.2.1), so the new shape admits every registered tag and refuses only words. Census of the head tree, non-test code, quoted values on `locale` / `defaultLocale` / `fallbackLocale` / `supportedLocales` lines across `examples/**`, `packages/**`, `ui/**`, `skills/**`: `en`, `zh-CN`, `en-US`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, `zh`, `de-DE`, `pt-br`, `fr-FR`, `de-CH`, `de`, and `default` (the last only as `ui/packages/plugin-calendar` prop defaults handed to `Intl`, never to `LocaleSchema`). Bundle filenames: `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`. UI `builtInLocales`: `en zh ja ko de fr es pt ru ar`. No 4–8 letter primary subtag anywhere a shipped value lives; the test-file sweep finds only the plugin-auth pin itself, the new spec rows, and `i18n-label-resolver.test.ts` keys (`toString`, `valueOf`) that never reach `LocaleSchema`. Read against the regex: `zh-Hans-CN`, `es-419`, `en-US` pass (pinned at translation.test.ts:50, plugin-auth :127–132, parity :59); the 3-letter class (`yue-HK` pinned in all three files; `fil`, `haw`, `art-lojban` by the same clause) passes; an extension form (`en-US-u-ca-gregory`) passes since each subtag is 1–8 alphanumerics; a bare private-use `x-…` failed the old shape too (one letter) and none is in use. `Chinese`, `English`, `Japanese`, `chinese-CN`, `null` are refused with `invalid_format` and a message naming the shape and the release (translation.test.ts:58–71); `Chinese` is refused at the item door at path `locale` only and as a bundle key (:80–82, :91). The refusal text (translation.zod.ts:37–42) now says `2–3`, names `Chinese` and says "write the tag, not the name" — each sentence is true of the code under it; it carries no tracker number.

**Byte-identity.** On the head, `git grep` for the shape finds exactly three `{2,3}` copies — translation.zod.ts:35, sys-user.object.ts:39, recipient-locale.ts:115 — and all three read `^[A-Za-z]{2,3}(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$`. The parity test's source-equality half (`LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE.source` against the string, flags `''`, parity :48–56) is unchanged and still the assertion that cannot miss a divergence. Left behind, and exactly the three the dev named: plugin-hono-server `current-user-endpoints-localization.test.ts:69` (a fixture row), `ui/packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx:224` (the no-`Intl` fallback), `ui/.../previews/doc-draft.ts:28` (add-locale hygiene). Judged each in ③. Two other `{2,3}` regexes on the head (`packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts:118`, `ui/.../machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts:199`) are different grammars for different jobs, not copies.

**The two contrary pins.** The seat's reading of the 2026-09-03 ruling holds: the ruling's quoted clause is "a malformed value is refused loudly by the column's BCP-47 shape check … and never dead-letters a notification", a shape check with no subtag length fixed; the quotation stays verbatim in the plugin-auth header (:4–11) and in the parity header (:7–14). The rewritten plugin-auth pin (:205–217) refuses `Japanese` with `VALIDATION_FAILED` AND accepts `tlh-QQ`, so it still guards "shape, not membership" and the ruling's second clause (an unknown tag falls to the ladder's floor rather than dead-lettering); its comment explains the width honestly. The rewritten parity pin (:72–84) inverts `null` on both sides and keeps `normalizeRecipientLocale('null')` undefined; `NOTHING_LITERALS` stays (recipient-locale.ts:122) and the docblock (:99–109) now says truthfully that it no longer changes an answer and is kept as the read side's own floor against a future widening. Both pins still guard what the ruling protects.

**ADR-0087.** The disposition `not-required (already-registered translation-locale-non-tag-refused)` is the honest one: the entry exists at the merge base and at the head, the gate's rule for that category is exactly those two facts (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:143–146, 5166–5190), and CI ran it with `--base` inside `Check Changeset` (pr-automation.yml:1017–1018), success at 15:12:36Z. Editing the registered D3 entry is legitimate here: it is the same major (18), the same retirement family and the same prescription (rewrite a language name by hand); the edit changes one number in `replacement` so the sentence matches the shape it describes, which is a correction, not the reversal Prime Directive 13 reserves for a new ADR; D4 projections are generated at publish, so no committed artifact goes stale (the dev's `check:generated` all-current reading is consistent with that); `check-closed-ceremony-text.mjs` pins a different entry only. Coverage: the entry's `surface` names translation items, bundle keys, the i18n configuration, seed datasets and the seed loader — the metadata surfaces — and its conversion lists a stored `Chinese` translation row as a TODO through `LocaleSchema`. It does NOT name `sys_user.locale`, and it cannot: a user row is data, not `sys_metadata`, so `os migrate meta --stored` never sees it and ADR-0087 has no reach there by construction. What covers a stored `sys_user.locale = 'Japanese'` row is the code, read: the delivery side normalizes it to `undefined` and falls to the deployment default (recipient-locale.ts:130–135, 148–163), the current-user endpoint falls to the next rung (hono test :232–240 pins the class), `checkFormat` skips an update that omits the field (rule-validator.ts:4606), and a re-send of the value is refused loudly. The ruling's two properties hold for stored rows with no migration entry owed. The changeset's prose on this point is judged in ③.

**Declarations.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` appear line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. `no (narrowing)` is the legal spelling for a published accept set that shrinks (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `no (widening)` is the malformed pair), identical to the shipped precedent `.changeset/25822-locale-tag-shape.md` (read at `27f38ada^`). `Skills-docs: none` is verified: `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx:22–24` and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx:244–246` already say a language name is refused at parse (this diff makes that true), `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` names only tag-shaped codes (`zh-CN` ×19, `en` ×17, `ja-JP`, `pt-BR`, `en-US`, `es-ES`, `zh`), and no page under `content/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/skills/**` or `docs/**` states the old `2–8` width.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, with the BREAKING banner, a FROM → TO fix and the ADR-0087 marker. Agreed. The kind is `narrowed`, and the rule is that a kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves: spec's `LocaleSchema` accept set shrinks; platform-objects' exported `SYS_USER_LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN` value and the `locale_bcp47_shape` rule tighten; service-messaging's exported `LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE` value tightens. No `major` (the repo ships none), and `Check Changeset` is green. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind for a value newly refused; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` keeps the BREAKING banner on a non-widening change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation: Clause-② corrected from the dispatch's `yes (narrowing)` to `no (narrowing)`.** Answered: correct. The seat rule and the shipped 25822 precedent both spell a narrowing of a published accept set as `no (narrowing)`; the claim 6442902707 records the correction.

- **Dev flag: hono-server fixture not moved** (`current-user-endpoints-localization.test.ts:69`). Reason holds in behaviour: the test's own docblock says what is under test is that the endpoint evaluates whatever rule the registry hands it, and every stored value it iterates (`Chinese (Simplified)`, `undefined`, `zh_CN!`, `42`) fails both widths, so none of the 13 cases turns on `{2,8}`. It was outside the claim's file surface, so leaving it was the right act under "stop on breach". One sentence in that fixture's docblock (:59–60, "The column's own rule, as the registry hands it to the endpoint — the `validations[]` entry `sys-user.object.ts` declares") is now stale: the fixture carries a string the column no longer declares. Non-blocking; a note for the plugin-hono-server lane to import `SYS_USER_LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN` or restate the fixture as a stand-in.
- **Dev flag: `ui/packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx:224` not moved.** Reason holds: the main branch is `Intl.getCanonicalLocales`, whose grammar admits a 5–8 letter language subtag, so narrowing only the fallback would make the two branches disagree on the same input; it reads a UI language preference, not stored metadata, and a word finds no pack. Outside this contract. Noted, not filed, as the dev recorded.
- **Dev flag: `doc-draft.ts:28` not moved.** Reason holds: the doc's `translations` map is `z.record(z.string(), …)` (doc.zod.ts:136–138), a different contract keyed by any string. Outside this contract. The same silent-key class remains in that add-locale box for the ui lane; noted, not filed.
- **Reviewer flag: the changeset's Fix bullet.** "`os migrate meta --stored` lists a stored row as a TODO (D3 entry `translation-locale-non-tag-refused`) and you rewrite it by hand" is true of a stored **translation** row and not of a stored `sys_user.locale` row, which that command never reads (see ①, ADR-0087). The D3 id in the same sentence scopes it for a careful reader, and the stored-row behaviour for a user is the ruling's own (floor, loud refusal on re-send, no dead-letter), so no contract is violated and no entry is owed. Non-blocking: the owning seat should tighten "a stored row" to "a stored translation row" before this text ships as `CHANGELOG.md`, or carry the precision into the release notes. Likewise `Metadata-protocol: narrowed (… and a user's `locale` column)` over-includes a data-validation rule under the metadata-protocol kind; the kind is unchanged by it.
- **Reviewer flag: the spec shape is now narrower than the BCP-47 grammar.** By decision and said in the docblock (translation.zod.ts:27–32): the grammar's 5–8 letter language subtags have no registered member, so the spec trades an unregistered syntactic class for the refusal its own text promised. Consistent with Prime Directive 12 (reject at the producer, no consumer fallback) and with the entry's "syntax check only" sentence.

Still `in_progress` at the second read: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–7/8)`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Third read at 15:26Z, the one this record is posted on: `Build Core` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, every `Type Check ·` lane success, `Test Core (8/8)` success; still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/8)` through `(7/8)` and `Type Check UI`; nothing red or cancelled.
